attributes.title: Level 5

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓Do both parameters have their type set in the makeDonut function definition?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Where should the type of parameter be defined in the a function?


Solution: 

string should be added next to the colon in the first parameter of the makeDonut function definition.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 185: a Type was expected.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the first parameter in the makeDonut function takes a string argument.

subgroups.title: Debugging Functions with Parameters
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: String added next to colon in first parameter of makeDonut function definition.
validationItems.failureText: Try defining the type of argument that will be passed to the toppingName parameter in the makeDonut function.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ What symbol should be used to separate the string and image arguments in the makeDonut function call?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbol should be placed between arguments when a function is called?


Solution: 

A comma , should be added between the arguments in the parentheses on Lines 198 and 199.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Notice the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Lines 198 and 199: ‘,’ was expected.



Fix the bugs in the code so that when the makeDonut function is called, it passes string and image arguments to the function.

subgroups.title: Debugging Functions with Parameters
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: Comma , is added between the arguments in the parentheses on Lines 198 and 199.
validationItems.failureText: Try adding the symbol used to separate the 2 arguments in the makeDonut function call.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Where can the toppingImage and toppingName parameters be used inside the makeDonut function definition?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What should be replaced in the function definition so that when the function is called, the correct topping image is placed on the donut and the correct topping name is pushed to the user’s order?


Solution: 

toppingImage should replace the image parameter in sprites.create code and toppingName should be used inside the parentheses of the push code in the makeDonut function definition.
steps.instructions:
When the makeDonut function is called, only marshmallows are added to the user’s order and placed on the donut!


Fix the bugs in the code so that whenever the user says “y” to adding a topping, that topping image is added to the donut and pushed to the user’s order.

subgroups.title: Debugging Functions with Parameters
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: toppingImage added as image parameter in sprites.create code and toppingName added inside parentheses of the push code in makeDonut function definition.
validationItems.failureText: Try updating the image parameter in the sprites.create code and the element parameter in the push code.

subgroups.name: solve 4

steps.hints: ❓ What code is needed to call the makeDonut function with the arguments to add candy to the donut?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How is a function called in JavaScript?


Solution: 

makeDonut(“candy”, candy) should be added below // function calls.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, it only asks the user if they want marshmallows or sprinkles on their donut. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the project also asks the user if they want candy on their donut.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 5 of Purple Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about functions. Functions can be used to name a unique chunk of code that can be easily reused in a project. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 5:

badges.title: Function Junction
badges.description: Create and call functions that use different parameter types in JavaScript.

badges.title: Functional Thinking
badges.description: Create a new function, with or without parameters, in JavaScript.

badges.title: Calling All Functions
badges.description: Call a function, with or without parameters, in JavaScript.

badges.title: Time for a Change
badges.description: Change the border color of the countdown timer.

badges.title: Feeling Shifty
badges.description: Use the shift function to remove and return the first value in an array.

badges.title: Read the Manual
badges.description: Use a block comment to document a function.

badges.title: Free Fallin’
badges.description: Set the acceleration of a sprite to simulate gravity.
